title: The Dragon’s Daughter
text: “Gau!”
A little while later, the assistant finally stopped crying. The assistant’s monster is trying to approach the giant dragon’s carcass.
“You can’t do that. If you go near there now, you’ll end up with more than just a few scrapes.”
“Please… don’t go.”

Since the assistant is holding onto the monster’s tail, it seems the monster has given up on going to the giant dragon. Although she had stopped crying, it didn’t seem like she had gotten over her sadness just yet. She was snuggling up to the monster, as if sharing its grief.
“Are you on good terms with the monsters in these mountains?”
“I am near my dad’s lair, but…”
“I see… Since humans have meddled too much here now… it’d probably be best for us to move on.”
“If you’d like, why don’t you come with us?”
“Will you take care of me?”
“We can’t just say ‘goodbye’ and leave it at that, can we!”
“That’s true.”
Watching the exchange between me and my Father, my Assistant looked hesitant. To hesitate when Father is reaching out his hand like this—she really is just a child.
“Besides… I’m also someone you should hate.”
“…Huh?”
“The one who defeated your father was a Sword Hero known as one of the Four Holy Swords. I’m one of those heroes—Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero.”
The assistant glared at my Father, his wariness growing.
“Is it really appropriate to be talking about this?”
“I think it’s better than having you wander around looking for a place to die.”
“Big bro, you’re so cool!”
“Keel, please don’t interrupt.”
“Dad said that even if I die, I shouldn’t think about avenging him… but… you’re not the one I’m talking about!”

The Assistant seems to be glaring fiercely at the adventurers and villagers swarming around the giant dragon. I can’t say I don’t understand how he feels. He’s so furious that even if he slaughtered every single one of those people—who only worship the hero when things are going well, but then hurl insults and throw stones when things go south—it still wouldn’t vent his frustration.
“I… I have nowhere left to go…”
“Gau!”
Just then, a monster makes its presence known and calls out to the Assistant.
“Gau, gau gau!”
“Right… yeah, that’s right.”
It turns out the Assistant has the ability to understand monster speech. I know she’s a rare being who can translate the voices of the Filolial-sama, who are unable to speak human language.
“What’s that little one saying?”
“She wants to get stronger. This time, strong enough not to lose, just like her dad. So I want to… get stronger, too. So no one can take her away from me again…”
“Just like me! Wyndia-chan!”
“Yeah!”
“In that case, there are plenty of ways. A Hero’s abilities can even make monsters stronger. If you want it… I can help you. What do you say?”
My Father extends his hand to the Assistant. She stares at his hand, quietly closes her eyes, and then reaches out.
“I… want to become strong, no matter what it takes. For that, I’d even sell my soul to a demon!”
“A demon, you say… Well, nice to meet you. Um, you’re coming too, right?”
“Gau!”
The monster with dragon blood also reached out its hand to Father.
“Nice to meet you. What’s your name?”
“Gau?”
“That one doesn’t have a name yet.”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah, so—”
The assistant grabbed both hands of the monster she called her “little sister,” closed her eyes as if in prayer, and then replied.
“Just like Dad… and because I want it to grow up to be a strong dragon, I want it to inherit Dad’s name.”
“…Gau!”
In response to the assistant’s words, the monster nodded vigorously and let out a cry.
“Okay, nice to meet you. Gaelion.”
“Gau!!”
“So that dragon’s name was Gaelion.”
It seems my Father had extended an invitation to join the party to the assistants and the others.
“Huh? I can’t add Gaelion-chan to the party.”
“The monsters said the rules are different. They said you need a monster mark to tame them.”
“Do you have to bind monsters with a monster mark?”
“Apparently, they usually won’t take to you unless you raise them from an egg.”

“Thanks to Wyndia, we’ll get their consent… I wonder if making her a masked slave, like Keel, would make her stronger? Well, let’s get moving. Maybe we can go to a slave trader, or use Elena’s connections or something?”
“Looking forward to working with you from now on.”
“…Nice to meet you.”
When I spoke to my assistant, my Father gave me a puzzled look. Did something strange happen?
“……? Motoyasu-kun, you’ve been quiet—or rather, just answering normally—but how do you see Wyndia-chan?”
“She’s a little brat who reeks of dragons. What’s that got to do with anything?”
“‘What’s that got to do with anything’… Could it be that you’ve met this girl in the future?”
“That’s right. In the future, she was working as an Assistant to Filo-tan’s Doctor. She was taking care of monsters in the village run by your Father.”
The assistant is tilting her head. She’s probably trying to catch Father’s attention. I’m not falling for it.
“And she was the foster parent of the dragon that Father received. She even gave it the same name as before.”
“Do you know how she came to meet my future self?”
“I only heard it secondhand, so I don’t know the details.”
“Um… what’s your relationship with that girl, Filo-chan?”
“Well, that’s—”
Just as I was about to explain, the Assistant cut in. You’re not invited to this conversation.
“What are you guys talking about?”
“Well, you see. This guy’s name is Motoyasu, and like me, he’s one of the Four Holy Spear Heroes… but he came from the future. And apparently, in the future, Wyndia and I have already met.”
He’s looking at me like he can’t believe a word of it. Well, I don’t really expect someone who’s been touched by a dragon to believe me anyway.
“Hey! How come Wyndia gets to talk to the Spear Guy like it’s no big deal! I can’t even get him to listen to me unless I’m in this form!”
“It seems it’s hard unless you’re close to this girl named Filo… So, Motoyasu, what was your relationship with her?”
“I’m the foster parent of Gaelion, who’s Filo-tan’s Rival! Filo-tan will never lose!”

“Um… she’s a dragon’s daughter, she manages monsters, she’s the Assistant to the Doctor treating the girl Motoyasu likes, and she’s the foster parent of his Rival—that’s a lot of roles… Isn’t she actually pretty amazing?”

The assistant is tilting his head with an expression that says he doesn’t quite get it. Don’t play dumb—I know all about it. I know that Gaelion from the First World, whom this guy cherished, used to make fun of Filo-tan for not being able to fly.
“I don’t understand what this person is saying…”
“Gau?”
“Ah… yeah, don’t worry about it too much. Normally, girls aren’t even recognized by Motoyasu-kun, but Wyndia-chan is just someone he happens to notice as an exception.”
“I don’t get it.”
My father gave a complicated smile. Still…
“You smell like a dragon. You really ought to wash yourself more often.”
“What did you say! What’s wrong with being a dragon?! You’re the one who smells like Filolial-sama! It’s making my nose twist!”
“Ha! To be unable to appreciate the noble scent of Filolial-sama—you really are just a dragon’s daughter after all.”
The assistant’s face softened slightly. To be happy about being a dragon’s daughter… she’s crazy. I really don’t understand what’s so fun about that.
“Hmph! Dragons are the strongest of all monsters!”
“Filolial-sama is the strongest!”
“Filolial? She’s just a bird that can’t fly! How is she any different from a horse? Dragon riders are way cooler!”
“…It seems she wants to die.”

Father will probably step in, so I’d better go easy on her. What do you mean, “dragon rider”? You’re nothing but a lowly nobody who doesn’t even come close to Filolial-sama and his kind—at best, you can only flit about in the sky like a mosquito or a dragonfly. If it’s the sky, even Filo-tan can fly!
“Ah… so they were like oil and water…”
Father clutched his head. Is this really such a big deal?
And just like that, the carriage became noisy once again.
